submissions.findingTextShort: A randomized vehicle-controlled study found a skin-lightening signal from an alpha-bisabolol-containing topical cream, not from oral supplementation.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: In 28 women, an eight-week randomized vehicle-controlled study evaluated an alpha-bisabolol-containing topical cream and reported a skin-lightening signal. PubMed identifies the administration route as topical. The result is a cosmetic topical outcome and cannot support oral anti-inflammatory, systemic, or supplement efficacy claims.
submissions.populationContext: 28 women in a topical cosmetic study.
submissions.usageContext: Alpha-bisabolol-containing topical cream for eight weeks.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Route and indication are decisive; topical pigmentation evidence is not oral-systemic evidence.

submissions.findingTextShort: A healthy-volunteer topical irritation experiment found no significant anti-irritant effect or dose-response for alpha-bisabolol.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: In a healthy-volunteer experimental irritation model, topical alpha-bisabolol did not produce a significant anti-irritant effect and did not show a dose-response, while glycerol performed better. This null topical finding should remain visible alongside other skin outcomes and should prevent a generic anti-inflammatory claim.
submissions.usageContext: Topical experimental irritation model; not oral dosing.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Indication-specific null; does not establish absence of every topical effect but directly constrains generalized anti-irritant language.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 12-week topical cosmetic formulation containing 0.25% timosaponin AIII improved wrinkle parameters without observed dermatologic toxicity; this is not oral efficacy evidence.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A human cosmetic study applied a topical formulation containing 0.25% timosaponin AIII to facial skin for 12 weeks and reported improvement in wrinkle parameters without observed dermatologic toxicity. This supports only route- and formulation-specific topical skin outcomes and short-term topical tolerability. It cannot justify the profile's oral standardized-botanical-extract capsule framing or systemic efficacy.
submissions.usageContext: Topical 0.25% timosaponin AIII-containing cosmetic formulation for 12 weeks.
submissions.safetyContext: Short-term topical tolerability only; does not establish oral/systemic safety.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Formulation and route identity must be retained; oral GI/hemolysis cautions require separate compatible evidence.
